findings.title: Second `downsize` definition overrides the 4-arg version, breaking existing callers
findings.body: `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined at line 145 and then redefined as `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby has no overloading, so the second definition replaces the first. Existing callers that pass `(from, to, width, height, opts)` now bind `height` to `dimensions` and `opts` to the hash. That makes `dimensions` the integer height and drops the width entirely, so the resize target is wrong and ImageMagick gets a malformed geometry. Or it raises ArgumentError for a 5-arg call with opts. The first definition is dead code. Keep one signature and update the callers.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failures and may leave the image over the size limit
findings.body: The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored. If `convert` fails (missing binary, corrupt image), the loop still runs 5 times without changing the file. The oversized file is then passed to `Upload.create_for`, so the user sees a generic size error. Also, `tempfile.size` on a Ruby Tempfile can be stale after an external process rewrites the file, because of buffering and the cached size. The loop may then re-run needlessly or exit early. Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` and check the result.

findings.title: In-place downsize with identical source and destination, and the `[0]` frame selector
findings.body: `downsize` is called with `from == to == tempfile.path`. The downsize instructions use `from[0]`, which keeps only the first frame, so animated GIFs lose animation. The `allow_animation` branch is only taken if the temp path matches `/\.GIF$/i`. Upload tempfiles generally keep the extension, but for URL downloads this is not guaranteed. In the animated case, gifsicle with `--output` equal to the input is also questionable. In-place conversion also overwrites the original with no recovery if the conversion fails midway.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB download cap ignores site settings
findings.body: The API download limit is now a hardcoded `10.megabytes` instead of a site setting. The client-side limits in utilities.js are hardcoded to 10MB too. The admin-configured `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb` no longer drives the client checks. Attachments are now capped at 10MB on the client regardless of `max_attachment_size_kb`, and the 413 error message shows 10MB even for configured limits. Larger configured limits are silently blocked, and smaller ones are no longer enforced client-side.

findings.title: Client validation uses a fixed 10MB limit for all upload types
findings.body: `maxSizeKB` was `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so it was per-type (image or attachment). It is now a constant 10MB for both. Attachments with a smaller configured limit pass client validation and fail only on the server. The server-side enforcement in `Upload.create_for` is unchanged, so the user gets a late, less helpful error.
